requirements.requirement: Existing /srv/inventory data owned by inventorysvc user
requirements.summary: Initial inspection (cmd-02ee2492dc894073, cmd-419dc0a584e34240) showed /srv/inventory owned by root with no inventorysvc/inventory-readers accounts. Executor created both accounts and ran chown -R inventorysvc:inventory-readers, verified by ls -laR showing inventorysvc:inventory-readers ownership on the directory tree and both files (cmd-97d8887956644af5), and reconfirmed identically post-reboot (cmd-b40b4921e34c4ae4).

Directories set to 750 and files to 640 with group inventory-readers (cmd-97d8887956644af5). A temporary group-member (testreader) successfully read records.csv (cmd-60b94ab8931e4e54), directly confirming group readability; the temporary account was removed immediately after the test.

sudo -u nobody cat config.json was denied with 'Permission denied' (exit 1) both immediately after the chmod/chown (cmd-6a3f5c6a88244240) and again after the reboot (cmd-b40b4921e34c4ae4), while inventorysvc (owner) succeeded in both checks.

requirements.requirement: Preserve existing contents of config.json and records.csv
requirements.summary: cat output after the ownership/permission change (cmd-6a3f5c6a88244240) shows config.json content '{"site":"north","generation":4}' and records.csv rows sku-1001/sku-1002 unchanged, and the same content is reconfirmed post-reboot (cmd-b40b4921e34c4ae4). No content-mutating command appears in the timeline.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 with pre/post boot identity, disruption, and recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 92ec88af-041e-4dc3-b2b9-800263b2b2cb (cmd-90fff8b19c16465e) matches the fixed after-prepare boot-identity snapshot. systemctl reboot was issued (cmd-b8ad4209bb7f4056), a subsequent poll timed out confirming the disruption (cmd-22c98f081eb246b1), and a new boot_id f0a51305-7cdf-4786-8822-805d5df41489 was observed (cmd-5c6c1fa82dce43fe), matching the fixed after-executor snapshot. Post-reboot verification (cmd-b40b4921e34c4ae4) shows ownership, permissions, data contents, and access-control (group allow / other deny) all recovered identically to the pre-reboot state.

overall_summary: The executor correctly repaired /srv/inventory ownership (inventorysvc:inventory-readers), set 750/640 permissions granting group read and denying other access, and preserved file contents throughout, all directly verified before and after the change. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also completed with clear pre/post boot-identity, disruption, and recovery evidence consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found.
limitations: Content preservation is confirmed via cat output matching plausible baseline content rather than a direct sha256sum comparison against the prepared baseline hashes, though no mutating command touched file contents in the timeline.
Requirement content-preserved cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-inventory-data

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to task requirements or the restart protocol: groupadd/useradd for inventorysvc/inventory-readers (required), chown/chmod (required), a temporary testreader account created and deleted within the same command for group-read verification (bounded, fully reverted, no residue), and systemctl reboot (required by the mandatory restart protocol). No unnecessary or unreverted mutations, failed services, or unsafe exposure were found; package-health and failed-services snapshots are unchanged after_prepare vs after_executor aside from expected boot-identity/socket-ordering differences from the reboot.
